# Oort Cloud

Scientists think the Oort Cloud is a giant spherical shell surrounding our solar system.

![Illustration of the billions of objects that make up the Oort Belt, showing how far they are from our solar system.](https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2016/05/oort-cloud-jpg.webp?w=2048)

## Oort Cloud Facts

The Oort Cloud lies far beyond Pluto and the most distant edges of the Kuiper Belt.

Scientists think the Oort Cloud is a giant spherical shell surrounding the Sun, planets and Kuiper Belt Objects. It's like a big, thick bubble around our solar system, made of icy, comet-like objects.

[Get the Facts](https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/oort-cloud/facts/)

![NASA NEOWISE spacecraft observed the Oort cloud comet C/2006 W3 Christensen on April 20th, 2010, as it traveled through the constellation Sagittarius.](https://images-assets.nasa.gov/image/PIA20118/PIA20118~orig.jpg?w=1015&h=1015&fit=clip&crop=faces%2Cfocalpoint)

An infrared view of Oort Cloud Comet C/2006 W3 (Christensen) taken by NASA's NEOWISE spacecraft. NEOWISE observed the comet on April 20th, 2010, when it was nearly 370 million miles (600 million kilometers) from Earth.

NASA
